q: The birthday paradox and its information-theoretic content: a random hash function h: {0,1}^n → {0,1}^{n/2} will have a collision (h(x) = h(y) for x≠y) after drawing approximately how many random samples?
exp: Birthday paradox: collisions occur after ≈ √(2^{n/2}) = 2^{n/4}... wait, for an output of n/2 bits (2^{n/2} values), collisions occur after ≈ √(2^{n/2}) = 2^{n/4} samples. (Corrected: for output space of size N, collisions after ≈ √N = 2^{n/4} samples when N = 2^{n/2}.) This underlies birthday attacks on hash functions.
